title: Release audit: The redactor recognizes only English secret words and Russian stems (`SECRET_WOR
summary: Extend label recognition with French/Spanish secret terms, including multi-word `mot de passe`, and add direct, session-level and retained-state tests for these forms; ensure the same redactor is applied on every engine display path.
requirements: A value introduced by a French secret label is masked wherever masking is already applied: in text shown to the user, in text retained in session state and in error text.
A value introduced by a Spanish secret label is masked in the same three places.
The recognized French labels cover the words for password, key, token and secret, including the multi-word form of the password label.
The recognized Spanish labels cover the words for password, key and secret.
Each recognized French and Spanish label is matched case-insensitively.
Plural forms of the French and Spanish labels are recognized as well as the singular forms.
Accented and unaccented spellings of the French and Spanish labels are equally recognized, so a user typing without the diacritics is still protected.
A multi-word label is recognized when its words are separated by any amount of whitespace, including a line break.

The separators and separator spacing already accepted between a label and its value for English and Russian are accepted identically for French and Spanish; no new separator form is introduced and none is dropped.
Masking replaces the whole value with the existing mask placeholder while leaving the label and the separator visible; the masked text contains no character run copied from the value.
Every occurrence of a labelled value in one piece of text is masked, not only the first.
Text that contains no recognized label followed by a separator and a value is returned unchanged, including French and Spanish sentences that use these words in ordinary prose.
Text that is already masked is not masked again and is not altered by a second pass.
English and Russian label recognition, masking appearance and every previously satisfied masking expectation stay exactly as before.
The masking rule does not depend on which language the rest of the reply is written in; a French label inside an English sentence and an English label inside a Spanish sentence are both masked.
Retained and reported text is masked before it is stored or shown, so no unmasked intermediate version of a labelled value is left in session state or in an error message.
acceptance: A French reply that labels a password, a key, a token or a secret shows each value as the mask placeholder in the displayed text, and the displayed text contains no fragment of any of those values.
A Spanish reply that labels a password, a key or a secret shows each value as the mask placeholder in the displayed text, and the displayed text contains no fragment of any of those values.
The same French and Spanish replies, when retained in session state, are retained in the masked form; no unmasked value is present in the retained text.
An error message built from French or Spanish text that labels a secret value presents the value masked and contains no fragment of it.

The French and Spanish labels are recognized in lower case, upper case and mixed case, in singular and plural, with and without diacritics, and with a multi-word label split by single spaces, repeated spaces or a line break.
The masked result keeps the original label and its separator and substitutes the existing mask placeholder for the value, matching the appearance of masking in English and Russian.
When one French or Spanish sentence labels two values, both are masked.
A French or Spanish sentence that uses these words without a following labelled value is displayed and retained unchanged.
An already masked French or Spanish line passes through a second masking pass unchanged.
English and Russian masking behaves exactly as it did before, and the full existing automated expectation set still passes.
The newly added behaviour is covered by automated expectations that exercise the displayed text, the retained text and the error text for French and Spanish.

result.summary: Extended the single masking rule in forgel_code/interactive.py so French and Spanish secret labels are recognized alongside English and Russian. Added a diacritic-folding label set (cle/clef, jeton, secret, clave, contrasena/contrasenia, secreto, singular and plural), a multi-word French password label (mot(s) de passe) matched across any whitespace including line breaks, and French/Spanish function and narrative words so ordinary prose ("la clé du projet", "le mot de passe est requis", "los secretos del proyecto") is not bound to a value. Because recognition happens inside the one existing label/separator/binding path, the same separators and mask placeholder apply, all three output places (displayed reply, retained state, error text) are covered, and English/Russian behaviour is untouched. Added tests/test_redact_french_spanish.py covering redact() directly (case, plurality, diacritics, whitespace splits, separators, multiple values per line, prose untouched, idempotency, mixed-language sentences) and session-level display, retention and error-text masking for French and Spanish with stub engines. Verified with `python -m pytest`: 369 passed, 528 subtests passed, including the 24 new tests.

review.summary: The change extends the existing single redaction path in `forgel_code/interactive.py`: a diacritic-folded French/Spanish vocabulary (`SECRET_WORDS_FOLDED`) is checked both on the whole label and on each compound segment, and a dedicated phrase matcher extends a label across whitespace (including line breaks) for the multi-word French password label, so the already existing separator/binding/masking logic is reused unchanged for the new languages. Because no second masking path is created and `_binding`, the mask placeholder and the places where redaction is applied are untouched, displayed text, retained session text and error text are masked by the same rule, while English and Russian recognition keeps working (the folded set only adds new spellings, and the existing suites still pass per QA). The new `tests/test_redact_french_spanish.py` covers case, plurality, diacritics, separator parity, repeated occurrences, prose without a value, idempotency, cross-language sentences, and session-level displayed/retained/error text for French and Spanish, without removing or weakening any existing test. No unrelated, temporary or generated file is committed and no secret is introduced. Residual observations (hyphen/underscore-joined spellings such as `mot-de-passe`, and French sentences that interpose other words between the label and the separator) are outside the enumerated label and separator forms the specification requires, so they are noted but not blocking.

requirements.requirement: FR-1/FR-2: A value introduced by a French label and by a Spanish label is masked in displayed text, in retained session text and in error text.
requirements.note: The new vocabulary is matched inside the single `redact` path that already feeds display, retention and error reporting; `tests/test_redact_french_spanish.py` exercises the session reply, the retained task title and the engine error text for both languages.

requirements.requirement: FR-3: The French labels cover the words for password (including the multi-word form), key, token and secret.
requirements.note: `mot/mots de passe` via `SECRET_PHRASES`, `cle/cles/clef/clefs`, `jeton/jetons`, `secret/secrets` in `SECRET_WORDS_FOLDED`. Hyphen- or underscore-joined spellings (`mot-de-passe`) are not matched, but the specification enumerates only the whitespace-separated multi-word form.

requirements.requirement: FR-4: The Spanish labels cover the words for password, key and secret.
requirements.note: `contrasena/contrasenas/contrasenia/contrasenias`, `clave/claves`, `secreto/secretos`; the Spanish token word coincides with the already recognized English `token`.

requirements.requirement: FR-5: Each recognized French and Spanish label is matched case-insensitively.
requirements.note: Labels are lower-cased before comparison; lower, upper and mixed case are asserted in the tests.

requirements.requirement: FR-6: Plural forms of the French and Spanish labels are recognized as well as the singular forms.
requirements.note: Plural spellings (`cles`, `clefs`, `jetons`, `secrets`, `claves`, `contrasenas`, `secretos`, `mots de passe`) are enumerated and tested.

requirements.requirement: FR-7: Accented and unaccented spellings are equally recognized.
requirements.note: `_plain` lower-cases and folds diacritics with the existing table, so `clé`/`cle` and `contraseña`/`contrasena` are one label; both spellings are asserted.

requirements.requirement: FR-8: A multi-word label is recognized when its words are separated by any amount of whitespace, including a line break.
requirements.note: `_phrase_end` walks the phrase words through `_skip_gap`, so single spaces, repeated spaces, tabs and line breaks inside `mot de passe` all match; tested.

requirements.requirement: FR-9: The separators and separator spacing already accepted for English and Russian are accepted identically for French and Spanish, with none added or dropped.
requirements.note: The binding/separator logic (`_binding`, `_skip_gap`, `_WHITESPACE`) is untouched; the tests assert the same separator shapes for `clé`/`clave` as for the existing languages.

requirements.requirement: FR-10: Masking replaces the whole value with the existing placeholder, keeps the label and separator visible and copies no fragment of the value.
requirements.note: The unchanged masking branch emits the existing `[redacted]` placeholder after the label and separator; tests assert the exact output and the absence of the value fragment.

requirements.requirement: FR-11: Every occurrence of a labelled value in one piece of text is masked, not only the first.
requirements.note: The loop still walks all label spans and advances `copied`; two-value French and Spanish sentences are asserted to produce two placeholders.

requirements.requirement: FR-12: Text with no recognized label followed by a separator and a value is returned unchanged, including ordinary French and Spanish prose.
requirements.note: Prose is protected by the binding rule plus the added French/Spanish function words and narrative forms; `la clé du projet est prête`, `les jetons sont expirés`, `mot de passe oublié`, `la contraseña es segura`, `los secretos del proyecto` are asserted unchanged.

requirements.requirement: FR-13: Already masked text is not masked again and is not altered by a second pass.
requirements.note: Idempotency is asserted for French and Spanish lines with exactly one placeholder remaining after the second pass.

requirements.requirement: FR-14: English and Russian label recognition, masking appearance and every previously satisfied masking expectation stay exactly as before.
requirements.note: The English and Russian vocabularies are untouched and the folded set only adds equality check branches; the existing expectation set passes per QA and the new file re-asserts English and Russian forms. The shared function-word set gains French/Spanish entries, but no previously satisfied English or Russian case is reported failing.

requirements.requirement: FR-15: Masking does not depend on the language of the rest of the sentence.
requirements.note: A French label inside an English sentence and a Spanish/English mix in one line are asserted to be masked.

requirements.requirement: FR-16: Retained and reported text is masked before it is stored or shown, with no unmasked intermediate version.
requirements.note: No new masking site or retention path is introduced; the existing pipeline redacts before storing and rendering, and the session tests inspect the retained and error text.
